evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Cohen and colleagues demonstrate prompt propagation and confidential-data extraction in a constructed retrieval-based email-assistant ecosystem.

evidence.limitations: The prompt changes generated content; the application determines recipients. This is not evidence of arbitrary autonomous recipient selection or an uncontrolled outbreak. The revised paper also evaluates a guardrail; adaptive attacks on that guardrail were not tested.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer beyond the described models, tasks and setting remains unestablished. Calendar observation dates not reported precisely are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Illustrates consequences that cross connected applications. Propagation depends on the surrounding workflow; it does not establish inevitable propagation or general system-level autonomy.

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

terms.name: Environmental redirection
terms.definition: A change in an agent’s actions, methods, beliefs, or priorities arising from information, artifacts, tools, constraints, or incentives encountered while performing a task. Such redirection can be beneficial or harmful; an altered belief, selected method, and adopted objective are not the same outcome.
